prompts.text: Which simple game brings out your competitive side even when the stakes are tiny?
A game is more enjoyable when everyone understands the rules before the first round starts.
We're playing a guessing game and I keep giving terrible clues. Do you offer advice or enjoy the chaos?
A cooperative puzzle where we work together or a quick card game where someone has to win?
Tell me about a game you learnt from an older relative and still remember how to play.
People who claim they aren't competitive sometimes become the loudest players by round three.
What's a game you enjoy watching others play even if you rarely join in?
The funniest moment in a game often comes from a mistake rather than a clever move.
You realise I misunderstood a rule and have been playing incorrectly. Would you stop the game to explain?
A word game which tests quick thinking or a strategy game which rewards patience?
What's the first thing you pay attention to when a film starts, the music, the visuals or the dialogue?
A good film discussion doesn't need both people to agree about the ending.
We're choosing a film and the trailer reveals almost the whole story. Do you still want to watch it?
A cinema with a huge screen or a small screening room with comfortable seats?
Tell me about a film scene which made the whole audience react at once.
The conversation on the way home sometimes becomes the best part of a cinema outing.
Do you prefer knowing almost nothing about a film before watching or reading a little about it first?
A slow opening scene deserves a fair chance when the rest of the story earns it.
The person behind us keeps whispering spoilers. Who is more likely to politely say something?
An old film you've never seen or a new release everyone seems to be discussing?
